insights.claim: Notebook workbench images deliberately disable all built-in authentication, making them entirely dependent on correct platform sidecar injection for access control.
insights.reasoning: The kustomize StatefulSet template sets --ServerApp.token='' and --ServerApp.password='', meaning any direct access to port 8888 bypasses authentication. If the oauth-proxy sidecar is not correctly injected by odh-notebook-controller, the workbench is unauthenticated. This is a deliberate design choice but represents a safety-critical coupling.

insights.claim: Code-server workbenches implement idle culling through an nginx/httpd/CGI shim that translates code-server healthz responses into Jupyter-compatible kernel API responses.
insights.reasoning: The culling API compatibility shim at /api/kernels/ allows odh-notebook-controller to use a single polling mechanism for both JupyterLab and code-server workbenches, despite code-server not natively exposing a Jupyter kernel API. This architectural bridge enables unified idle detection across IDE types.

insights.claim: Notebook images bundle pycryptodome alongside the FIPS-capable system OpenSSL, creating a mixed cryptographic environment where user code may use non-FIPS-validated crypto primitives.
insights.reasoning: While the UBI9 base image and compat-openssl11 provide FIPS-capable OpenSSL, pycryptodome (v3.23.0) is a pure-Python/C cryptographic library that does not use the system FIPS provider. User code or transitive dependencies that import pycryptodome instead of the cryptography library will operate outside FIPS validation.
